title: Thirty notebooks, five students
intro: Thirty identical notebooks are given out to five students, P, Q, R, S and T.
clues: Every notebook is given to one of the five students.
Each student gets at least 2 notebooks.
P gets more than Q, Q gets more than R, R gets more than S, and S gets more than T.

questions.stem: What is the greatest number of notebooks P can get?
why: P gets the most when the others get as few as the rules allow: T 2, S 3, R 4, Q 5.

questions.stem: What is the least number of notebooks P can get?
why: P is the largest of five different whole numbers adding to 30. With P = 7 the most possible is 7 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 = 25, too few.

questions.stem: In how many different ways can the notebooks be given out?
why: Start everyone at the smallest staircase: P 6, Q 5, R 4, S 3, T 2 (20 notebooks). The other 10 are extras, and the order stays strict exactly when the extras never increase from P down to T.
So count the ways to split 10 into at most five parts: by largest part 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 there are 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 4, 1. Total 30.

questions.stem: If R gets exactly 6 notebooks, in how many different ways can the notebooks be given out?
why: With R = 6, S and T are at most 5 and at least 2, with T below S: (S, T) = (3, 2), (4, 2), (4, 3), (5, 2), (5, 3), (5, 4). P and Q share 24 - S - T, with Q at least 7 and P above Q.
P + Q = 19 gives 3 ways, 18 gives 2, 17 (twice) 2 each, 16 gives 1 and 15 gives 1: 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 11.

questions.stem: If Q gets exactly twice as many notebooks as T, how many notebooks does P get?
why: Let T get t, so Q gets 2t, and S and R fit strictly between t and 2t. t = 2 leaves only 3 between 2 and 4, not room for two. t = 3 gives S 4, R 5, Q 6 and P 30 - 18 = 12, which works.
With t = 4 or more, P is at most 27 - 5t, which is 7 or less, while Q = 2t is 8 or more: impossible. So P gets 12.

steps: A strict order with a minimum makes a staircase: the smallest distribution is P 6, Q 5, R 4, S 3, T 2, using 20 of the 30. Every way of giving out the notebooks adds 10 extras without breaking the order.
For the most one student can get, push everyone else to their least: P can reach 16 (T 2, S 3, R 4, Q 5).
For the least P can get, make the five numbers as close as possible: 8, 7, 6, 5, 4. For counting questions, fix one student's amount and count the rest, or count the splits of the extras.
